title: The north rises. Perhaps this was what the Pope had counted on. On New Year's Day 1405 the Portuguese lands proclaim a Kingdom of Estremadura and La Mancha and the Madrid country rise again as a Kingdom of Toledo; the next day the Leonese of Shalamanka rise against their Naṣrid ṭāʾifa as Ciudad Rodrigo. Forty-eight towns of the crown and sixteen of Shalamanka go over; Toledo, Lisbon and Setúbal hold

title: The Emperor Saʿd is dead. On the eve of Ramaḍān, marching his army through Moya against the risers of the north, the conqueror of half the peninsula dies at fifty-seven, after forty-one years on the throne. A death answers many questions he still wished to ask; his son Ismāʿīl takes the throne, and the question of the grandsons is no longer his

data.place: on the march through Moya, in the Ṭāʾifa of Qūnka
data.gameNotice: His strong character made our country a more honest place

title: Ismāʿīl ibn Saʿd, thirty-eight, is proclaimed Emperor and Sultan of al-Andalus on his father's death. By the law of primogeniture his heir is his eldest son Muḥammad; Bernarda of Mursiyya is his consort; his brother Yūsuf takes his old seat in the dīwān, promoting Andalusī culture

data.ruler: Ismāʿīl ibn Saʿd, born 8 March 1366 (47/100/38), deceitful, goal-oriented
data.heir: Muḥammad ibn Ismāʿīl, born 25 October 1385 (16/20/17), with three children of his own

source: Trent's accession notice; save of 31 March 1405

title: The new Emperor's first battle. Sixteen days after his father's death, the so-called King of Toledo attacks Ismāʿīl's army before Qūnka with 5,085 men against 4,897. He loses 3,258 of them; the Emperor loses 300
